headline: Learned models for tumor fraction, clonality, and foundation-model benchmarking in omics
label: Learned Models For Biomedical Data
summary: Foundation models and Bayesian deep learning are being benchmarked against simple baselines and applied to cfDNA, flow cytometry, and single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned models applied to high-dimensional biological measurements, with evaluation against realistic data as a central concern. VCBench reports that linear baselines match or beat most single-cell foundation models across five testable dimensions, and a tabular foundation model study on gut microbiome data reports in-context robustness to perturbed queries, with zero-imputation the most harmful. Simulation-trained Bayesian deep learning (purNPE) estimates tumor fraction in cell-free DNA with uncertainty, and DEEPctMUT adds deep learning noise filtering to tumor-naive ctDNA mutation calling. EventHorizon pretrains a self-supervised transformer on 100,937 unlabeled clinical flow cytometry specimens. A microbial network benchmark similarly finds that synthetic SPIEC-EASI data diverges from real and perturbed microbiome data. What is new is the pairing of large-scale pretraining or simulation with explicit stress tests against baselines and realistic distribution shift.
